runtime: go1.24.7 linux/amd64, GOAMD64=v1, GOGC=100 (default), GOMEMLIMIT=off (default), GOMAXPROCS=4, CGO_ENABLED=1, one child process per parser

results.notes: gojson.Unmarshal into Event: copies the frame into a pooled, NUL-terminated context buffer inside the call; decoded strings are copied out of it. alloc_bytes_per_event, allocs_per_event, gc_count, gc_ms and gc_cpu_ms come from a separate untimed pass: as many rounds as were measured, over the preloaded lines, with no frame copies, so they cover the parses only
results.objects_note: Strings of up to 512 bytes are copied into a per-context arena of chunks up to 16 KiB that many events share, so they add almost no objects (a kept event keeps its arena chunk alive, shared with its neighbours); a retained event is the Event, the tags slice and one slice per tag. Retained objects are MemStats.HeapObjects, which counts each 16-byte tiny-allocator block once: pointer-free allocations under 16 bytes (short strings such as "root" or a short relay URL) share blocks, so retained objects can be a little lower than the allocations kept alive, while allocs_per_event counts every allocation

results.notes: generated decoder (easyev/event_easyjson.go, -no_std_marshalers) via easyjson.Unmarshal. alloc_bytes_per_event, allocs_per_event, gc_count, gc_ms and gc_cpu_ms come from a separate untimed pass: as many rounds as were measured, over the preloaded lines, with no frame copies, so they cover the parses only
results.objects_note: Retained objects are MemStats.HeapObjects, which counts each 16-byte tiny-allocator block once: pointer-free allocations under 16 bytes (short strings such as "root" or a short relay URL) share blocks, so retained objects can be a little lower than the allocations kept alive, while allocs_per_event counts every allocation

results.notes: one reused fastjson.Parser: ParseBytes copies the frame into the Parser's own reused buffer and the tree points into it; strings are unescaped lazily, only when read. The tree is only valid until the next Parse, so retained heap is null. alloc_bytes_per_event, allocs_per_event, gc_count, gc_ms and gc_cpu_ms come from a separate untimed pass: as many rounds as were measured, over the preloaded lines, with no frame copies, so they cover the parses only
results.objects_note: No retained count: the tree lives in the reused Parser and is overwritten by the next parse. allocs_per_event is 0 once the Parser's buffers have grown to fit
